title: Tissue Engineering: Construction of a Multicellular 3D Scaffold for the Delivery of Layered Cell Sheets
protocol: Dissolve 2.6 g of pNIPAAM in 2 ml of a 60% toluene/40% hexane solution.
Heat the mixture to 60 °C for 10 min, stirring until the pNIPAAM is dissolved.
Cut filter paper into a 60 mm diameter circle and place it in the Buchner funnel.
Filter the solution through the Buchner Funnel into the pre-weighed glass beaker.
Place the beaker and contents into a bell vacuum (24 psi) overnight for 16 hours.
Weigh the beaker to establish the weight of the pNIPAAM residue.
Add isopropyl alcohol to the pNIPAAM residue, creating a 50/50 w/w solution.
Place 2 ml of the pNIPAAM-isopropyl alcohol solution on the surface of the tissue culture plate.
Coat the plate for 5 min under UV light.
Wash the plate with 2 ml of warm PBS twice before using it for cell culture.
Incubate cells at 37°C for a minimum of 24 hours to achieve confluence.
Subject plates to temperatures below 32°C to release cell sheets.
Transfer the cell sheet to a strong base fibrous matrix containing a neovascular permissive hydrogel with vascular endothelial cells.
Isolate the cell population according to individual derivation procedures.
Wash cells with 2 ml of warm PBS.
Add 3 ml of trypsin to the cells for 5 min.
Inhibit trypsin by adding 3 ml of culture media or PBS containing 10% FBS.
Collect the cells in a conical tube and count an aliquot.
Spin the cells at 1,000 rpm (228 x g) for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in growth media.
Place the media containing cells on a 35 mm thermo-sensitive plate coated with pNIPAAM.
Place the prepared matrix into an incubator at 37 °C O/N.
Cut the pre-sterilized matrix into a desired size and shape.
Collect endothelial cells and disperse into a single cell solution using 1x trypsin.
Deactivate trypsin enzyme using an equal amount of soybean trypsin inhibitor or 10% FBS in PBS.
Collect solution/cells into a 15 ml conical tube.
Count cells and calculate volume needed for patch dimensions.
Extract 2 million cells and place them into a new 15 ml conical tube.
Spin the cell suspension at 228 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate supernatant, leaving cells as a pellet in the tube.
Mix HA and Gelatin liquid materials in a 1:1 ratio.
Add 80% of total volume into the conical tube containing the cell pellet.
Resuspend endothelial cells in the 1:1 HA/Gelatin mixture.
Place suspended cells in the HA/Gelatin mixture into the base fibrous matrix from Step 2.
Add 1/5 (20 percent) of the total volume desired of the cross-linker.
Incubate for 1 hour at 37 °C.
Remove 35 mm pNIPAAM-treated plates containing cells from incubator and place in cell culture hood at RT.
Aspirate media from cells.
Add 2 ml of 6% normal gelatin heated to 37 °C.
Place metal lattice into the warm gelatin, submerging it below the surface.
Place entire plate onto ice for 5 to 7 minutes.
Use a spatula to carefully separate the gelatin edges from the side of the plate.
Use forceps to lift the metal lattice from the plate.
Move the cell sheet to the dish and place it on top of the base fibrous matrix-hydrogel combination.
Add 2 ml of warm media (37 °C).
Incubate O/N allowing the sheet of cells to adhere to the hydrogel surface.
Remove the metal lattice after the solution warms (approximately 1 hr), or the next day.
